ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7), noting the driver was still 1685 m from the pickup point when the rider cancelled; no account flag.

rejected_claims.reason: The claim that this over-charge is a further instance of the same no-show conduct and that RD-6/NS-2 require a flag fails: RD-6 requires a route-deviation finding with route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1, and there is no off-route segment here [F15][RD-6]; NS-2's flag requires the driver to have pressed "I'm Here" while GPS shows him off the pickup point, but no tap was ever made [F4][NS-2]; profile facts may not alone decide the case [F15][RD-6].

To the extent it asks the judge to weigh the driver's 666 trips / 2 upheld no-show history as conduct evidence on the merits, it fails: profile facts cannot alone decide a case [F15][RD-6], and no clause makes trip volume or unrelated upheld no-shows a defence to the NS-4 timing rule [F2][NS-4]; the driver side itself concedes the fee fails.

Invokes NS-1/NS-3, but NS-3 is not engaged: the cancellation was made by the rider, not the driver [F2][NS-0], so the driver-cancellation branches do not apply [F2][NS-3]; the point is correct only as corroboration of F1/F3 [F10][NS-1].

Relies on the late-ETA narrative as a legal ground via NS-1; Ryde has no late-ETA free-cancellation rule and NS-8 is informational, so the chat estimate is not itself a basis for the refund [F8][NS-4]; the refund rests on the sub-3-minute cancellation [F2][NS-4].

Correct as to outcome but its framing that the rider's "driver was nowhere near" ground is legally irrelevant goes only to NS-8-style late-ETA relief, not to NS-4: the 175-second timing alone is sufficient [F2][NS-4], and the GPS fact [F1] is what displaces any no-show defence [F1][NS-1].
